findings.title: POSITIVE control is a capacity/interaction test, not an order-matching test: chain arms have 480 trainable parameters with recurrent cross-type interaction, the bag has 224 and is purely additive
findings.evidence: Lines 91-95 `init`: W = K*(DE*H) = 4*40 = 160; U = K*(H*H) = 4*64 = 256 (`np.zeros((H, H)) if bag else rng.normal(...)`); b = K*H = 32; R = H*NCLS = 32. Chain total 480; bag trainable 224 (U frozen: line 129 `g["U"][j] = np.zeros((H, H))`, verified U stays exactly zero under the Adam update at lines 141-143). Line 101 bag forward: `h = sum(np.tanh(E[:, order[j], :] @ p["W"][j] + p["b"][j]) for j in range(K))` -- a sum over types, no term couples two types. Line 105 chain forward: `h = np.tanh(E[:, order[j], :] @ p["W"][j] + h @ p["U"][j].T + p["b"][j])` -- multiplicative interaction via U. The world (line 60) `s = np.tanh(E[:, t, :] @ A[j] + s @ B[j].T)` has the chain's exact functional form, so the matching chain is realizable and the bag is not. Line 204: `pos_ok = (A[cas][0] > A[bag][0] + 0.02) and (Cc[rev][0] > Cc[bag][0] + 0.02)` compares matching CHAIN vs BAG only. Commit: 'BAG mechanism-free loses by 0.13-0.15 everywhere ordered' while the MISMATCHED chains sit within 0.0219 / 0.0136 of the matching chain, i.e. a wrong-order chain still beats the bag by roughly 0.11-0.13.
findings.effect_on_conclusion: 'Order matters' in the commit is almost entirely 'a recurrent chain beats an additive bag' -- an asymmetry in parameter count (480 vs 224) and representational class, present with any order. The order-specific effect is only the +0.0219 / -0.0136 match-vs-mismatch gap. The positive control therefore does not certify that the harness can detect order-matching at the 0.02 scale it then uses as the verdict threshold.

findings.title: Conditions (a) and (c) are mirror images measuring the same quantity twice; the 0.02 threshold falls between the two realisations, so 'HELD' vs 'FAILED' is a threshold artifact
findings.evidence: Lines 181-182: `make_world(r, CAS_ORDER, n)` and `make_world(r, REVERSED, n)` with the same seeds 1000+sd (line 160). make_world (lines 51-54) draws A, B, C, E from the rng before the order is used, so (a) and (c) share identical A, B, C, E; only the composition order at line 60 differs (verified: `E identical=True`, label agreement 0.2113-0.3300 per seed). E's K type channels are i.i.d. (line 54 `E = rng.normal(0, 1, (n, K, DE))`), so relabelling types maps world-CAS/arm-CAS onto world-REV/arm-REV exactly in distribution. Both non-matching arms are full derangements in both worlds: verified `positions matched = 0/4` for REV and RANDFIX vs world CAS and for CAS and RANDFIX vs world REV. Lines 224-225: `d_a = A[cas][0] - max(A[rev][0], A[ran][0])` (>= +0.0219) and `d_c = Cc[cas][0] - Cc[rev][0]` (-0.0136). Line 232 thresholds `d_a > 0.02` and `d_c < -0.02`.
findings.effect_on_conclusion: Match-minus-mismatch was realised as >= 0.0219 in (a) and 0.0136 in (c); the registered 0.02 line sits between two draws of the same effect. That the sign pattern flips with the world's order actually supports 'the world sets the winner', but the HELD/FAILED labels the program printed reflect noise around a fixed constant, not a difference between the CAS order and the reversed order. The registered prediction (c) 'FAILED' is not evidence that CAS resists losing.

p6_lenses.world_generation_answer_key: The label is a deterministic function of the evidence E with no noise. Lines 48-62 `make_world`: per condition, A (K matrices DE x H), B (K matrices H x H), C (H x NCLS) and E (n x K x DE, i.i.d. normal type channels) are drawn from the seed BEFORE the order is used; then line 60 `s = np.tanh(E[:, t, :] @ A[j] + s @ B[j].T)` composes types in `true_order` and line 61 `y = np.argmax(s @ C, axis=1)`. The chain arm's forward (line 105) has exactly this functional form (W<->A, U<->B, R<->C, b=0), so the arm whose order equals the world's order is the generator itself (realizable); any other fixed order is a mismatch of equal capacity; the bag (line 101) cannot represent the cross-type interaction at all. The true order is swept as a condition (lines 180-185): (a) CAS (0,1,2,3), (c) REVERSED (3,2,1,0), (b) per-item random permutation (lines 72-77, no fixed order can match), NEG no-structure bag world (line 86). Consequences verified outside the repo: (a) and (c) share identical A, B, C, E for each seed (only composition order differs; label agreement 0.2113-0.3300); REVERSED and RANDOM_FIXED (2,0,3,1) both match 0/4 positions of both world orders, so both 'other' arms are full derangements; (b) makes all fixed orders exchangeable, so its tie is by construction. The world's true order is therefore the answer key: the arm that carries it wins by realizability, whichever order it is -- which is exactly what the script set out to show, but the design makes (a) and (c) two draws of one quantity rather than two independent tests.

findings.effect_on_conclusion: Neither control (lines 204-206) nor any of the three predictions (line 232) was evaluated on held-out data. Chain arms have 480 trainable parameters (my count: W=160 U=256 b=32 R=32) fitting 1500 points for 700 Adam steps; the bag has 224. findings.title: The POSITIVE control tests chain-vs-bag capacity, not order-matching: the bag loses by MORE in the world where no fixed order can match
findings.evidence: Line 204: pos_ok = (A[cas][0] > A[bag][0] + 0.02) and (Cc[rev][0] > Cc[bag][0] + 0.02). Line 26-27 claims this shows the test 'can detect order-matching'. But the bag (line 93: U = zeros; line 101: commutative sum, no recurrence) has 224 parameters vs 480 for each chain arm. Commit-message / untracked-repro numbers: (a) matching arm minus bag = 0.9689 - 0.8181 = 0.1508; (c) 0.9448 - 0.8212 = 0.1236; but in (b), where the per-item order (line 73) is unobservable and NO fixed order matches, every chain arm beats the bag by 0.7245-0.5689 = 0.1556, 0.7247-0.5689 = 0.1558, 0.7307-0.5689 = 0.1618. The chain-over-bag margin is largest precisely where order-matching is impossible, so the margin is not an order-matching signal. The order-matching signal proper is matching-chain minus non-matching-chain: +0.0219 in (a) and +0.0136 in (c), each within one seed sd (sds 0.0206/0.0272/0.0272 in (a); 0.0169/0.0561/0.0238 in (c), untracked repro stdout lines 12-20). The commit message's 'BAG loses by 0.13-0.15 everywhere ordered' is also imprecise: vs CAS in (c) it is 0.9312-0.8212 = 0.1100, and in (b) up to 0.1618.
findings.effect_on_conclusion: 'Both controls PASS' is not evidence that the instrument detects order-matching; the 'order matters' half of the conclusion rests on a capacity-confounded comparison measured on training data. The direction of the other half ('no CAS-specific advantage seen') is not contradicted by any number, but it is a null from an instrument whose positive control is vacuous for the property claimed. A capacity-matched mechanism-free baseline (e.g. an MLP on the flattened 20-dim evidence with ~480 params) was not registered.

findings.title: A one-line linear rule (OLS on the raw 20 evidence dims, 84 numbers, no hidden layer) reaches 0.71 on a genuine held-out set -- above every arm's held-out accuracy in the untracked repro -- so the registered mechanism-free baseline was not the cheapest

Single-slot OLS on held-out: (a) t=0..3: 0.4281 0.4024 0.4687 0.5519; (c) 0.5439 0.4816 0.3960 0.4245 -- the LAST-processed slot (t=3 in (a), t=0 in (c)) carries the most linearly readable label signal. This removes the remaining support for 'order matters' as a generalisation claim; it does not change the direction of 'no CAS-specific advantage detected'.

findings.title: World / answer-key check: no hidden channel to the label beyond test==train; the arms are architecturally identical to the generator, so 'order matters' is a property of the chosen world family
findings.evidence: Line 60 (world): s = np.tanh(E[:, t, :] @ A[j] + s @ B[j].T); line 105 (arm): h = np.tanh(E[:, order[j], :] @ p['W'][j] + h @ p['U'][j].T + p['b'][j]). Same recurrence, same H=8 (line 39), so the arm whose order equals true_order is an exact re-parameterisation of the teacher; non-matching arms are not. The true order (lines 181-184) is never passed to any arm: line 164-166 hands each arm only (order, Etr, ytr, Ete, yte), identical across arms. E is i.i.d. N(0,1) per slot (line 54) and y is a deterministic function of E, so there is no side channel. The three chain arms share identical init (line 165, seed 7000+sd; my check [6]: W identical); the bag's R differs because line 93 skips the U draws and shifts the RNG stream (minor asymmetry). Line 246-247 itself says 'ORDER IS A PROPERTY OF THE TASK'.
findings.effect_on_conclusion: No arm holds an answer key beyond the disclosed condition sweep. But the same builder chose a world family that is by definition an order-sensitive K-step tanh recurrence and an arm family that is that recurrence; 'order matters' for this family is true by construction and says nothing about any other task. Combined with the train==test defect, the experiment establishes neither 'order matters' nor 'CAS order has no value' as generalisation claims.

p6_lenses.world_generation_answer_key: The world's true order is a swept CONDITION (lines 181-184: CAS_ORDER, REVERSED, per-item random at line 73, and a bag world at line 86) and is never handed to an arm: run_condition (lines 164-166) gives every arm the same Etr/ytr/Ete/yte and only the arm's own fixed order. In condition (a) the CAS arm's order (0,1,2,3) equals the world's true order and in (c) the reversed arm's does -- this is the disclosed design, not a hidden key. E is i.i.d. N(0,1) per slot (line 54) and y = argmax(s @ C) is a deterministic function of E, so no content side channel exists (my single-slot OLS shows the last-processed slot is the most linearly readable: held-out 0.5519 for t=3 in (a), 0.5439 for t=0 in (c), but that is order structure, not a leak). The one true answer key is that the evaluation set IS the training set (lines 160-163; verified 20/20 identical). Secondary: arm recurrence (line 105) is architecturally identical to the generator recurrence (line 60), so the matching arm is an exact re-parameterisation of the teacher and 'order matters' holds for this world family by construction; and for the same seed, conditions (a), (c) and (b) share identical A, B, C and E (verified), differing only in composition order.
p6_lenses.registered_before_run_verifiable: No. The script's only commit is 1e58d7254d97c88effa609f7ad05ee2fca9b1aee (2026-09-02 21:29:49 -0700), and the results (0.9689, 0.9471, +0.0219, 0.9312, 0.9448, -0.0136, 0.7245, 0.7307, -0.0061, 0.0301) appear only in that same commit's message. The assertion 'written before running' exists in the docstring (lines 15, 17) and the printed banner (line 174) only; no prior commit, hash, or timestamped preregistration artifact exists. No run output was committed at all.
p6_lenses.held_out_is_held_out: NOT held out. Lines 160-162: `rng = np.random.default_rng(1000 + sd)` / `Etr, ytr = worldfn(rng, NTR)` / `Ete, yte = worldfn(np.random.default_rng(1000 + sd), NTE)  # same world, fresh draw`; line 163 `Ete, yte = Ete[:NTE], yte[:NTE]` is a no-op because line 40 sets NTR = NTE = 1500. Each worldfn draws A, B, C and then E (and, for the random world, the per-item permutations) from that single stream, so two fresh generators seeded with the same integer 1000+sd produce the same params, the same E and the same y. Verified by this audit with numpy (scratchpad check #1, exec of the committed blob's definitions only): np.array_equal(Etr, Ete) == True and np.array_equal(ytr, yte) == True for all 20 (condition, seed) pairs: (a), (c), (b), (NEG) x sd 0..4, shapes (1500, 4, 5). Consequently line 147-148 scores every arm on its own training data; every accuracy reported in the commit message is a training-fit number. The comment 'fresh draw' and the banner '1500 train / 1500 held out' (line 173) are false. Note the intended 'same world, fresh draw' cannot be produced by changing the seed with these function signatures, because a different seed also redraws A, B, C (a different world).
p6_lenses.arms_matched: Data: identical Etr/ytr/Ete/yte for all four arms per seed (lines 161-166). Optimiser: identical for all arms -- Adam-style with beta 0.9/0.999, eps 1e-8, LR = 0.05, STEPS = 700 full-batch (lines 40, 116, 139-146). Parameters (my count from init(), line 91-95): each chain arm W=160 U=256 b=32 R=32 total 480; BAG W=160 U=0 (line 93 zeros U, line 129 zero-grads it) b=32 R=32 total 224. Init: the three chain arms receive bit-identical initial W, U, b, R (line 165, default_rng(7000+sd)); the bag receives the same W but a different R because skipping the U draws shifts the RNG stream (verified: W identical True, R identical False) -- minor. Asymmetries that matter: (1) the BAG has 256 fewer parameters and no recurrence, so every chain-vs-bag margin (the POSITIVE control at line 204 and the commit's 'BAG loses by 0.13-0.15') is confounded with capacity, and the bag loses by MORE (0.1556/0.1558/0.1618) in world (b) where no order can be matched than in (a) 0.1508 or (c) 0.1236; (2) chain arms are architecturally identical to the world generator (line 105 vs line 60), so the order-matching arm is a teacher re-parameterisation; (3) only 3 of 24 fixed orders are arms; (4) all margins are training-fit, where the 480-parameter arms memorise 1500 points far above what an 84-number linear rule fits (0.7252 in (a)).
p6_lenses.verdict_on_specific_cas_order_value: NO VERDICT is licensed by this script. As committed, the script's own deterministic branch ends at lines 251-253 ('THE PREDICTION DID NOT HOLD AS REGISTERED') because d_c = -0.0136 fails the registered d_c < -0.02; the status CAS_PRECEDENCE_VALUE_NOT_ESTABLISHED (line 246) was never printed and lives only in the commit message. More fundamentally, every number is a training-fit accuracy (test set == training set, verified 20/20), the positive control is a capacity test rather than an order-matching test, and a genuine held-out check shows an 84-number linear rule at 0.7108/0.7092 (my measurement) that no arm is shown to beat out of sample (untracked repro: arm held-out max 0.6875 in (a), 0.6857 in (c), positive control FAIL). What survives as direction only: on training fit the CAS arm never beats the world-matching arm (d_c = -0.0136) and never beats the other fixed orders on random-order worlds (d_b = -0.0061), so nothing in the data points to a CAS-specific advantage -- but that is a null read from an instrument that cannot detect the property it was built to detect. Plain-English status: OPEN / NOT MEASURED. Neither 'P > C > E > O carries value' nor 'order matters but CAS order does not' is established by p6_order_test.py; the specific-CAS-order question remains untested until the held-out draw is repaired, a capacity-matched or linear mechanism-free baseline is registered, and a program (not prose) emits the status.
